---
title: "Specification menu"
subtitle: "The fourteen decisions, by group"
bibliography: [references.bib, references-new.bib]
---

This page sets out every decision that an analysis of the claim has to make, the options that each decision offers, and whether each option is a justifiable way of answering the claim. The claim, in the wording that SCORE took from the paper of the original author (OA) [@Teney2016DoesEUEconomic], is that "poor economic performances ... decrease positive dimensions of EU framing" (p. 619). The course reads it as a claim about change within countries over time, that is, about whether the citizens of a member state framed the EU less in positive terms than before as the economy of their country deteriorated, in the member states of 2004–2013. The [background page](background.qmd#sec-questions) sets out the hypothesis from which the claim was taken and the data on which it rests.

Fourteen decisions stand between those data and a verdict on the claim, and most of them offer more than one option that a competent analyst might choose. The course has asked of every option whether it is a justifiable way of answering this claim, and the options that are have been crossed into the 864 specifications of the curve of the claim, so that the disagreement that remains on the curve is disagreement between defensible analyses; each option that left the curve is given its reason below, with a link to the module that teaches it.

The decisions fall into three groups, and the menu is arranged by them. Decisions about **the question** change what is being estimated, so that two people who choose differently are answering different questions and their results are not rival estimates of one quantity. **Measurement** decisions change how a named quantity is measured and leave the question as it is. Decisions about **the model** change neither, only how the model is fitted and how uncertain its answer is said to be.

## The decision map {#map}

```{r}
#| include: false
# Data for the decision map, read once at render: every option of the full menu,
# the curve of the claim, the curve of the negative scales, every option set
# against its twins on the curve, and the titles of the pages that teach each
# option. All of it is aggregate. The pairs travel as three short arrays per
# option and test (twin on the curve, r of the alternative, p < 0.05 or not),
# which keeps the page small. The inference rules need no pairs, because the
# curve file carries every p-value.

axes <- c("outcome", "predictor", "copredictor", "estimator", "sample", "weights",
          "construction", "noop", "item_set", "cell_weight", "measure", "pred_form", "family")
vary <- c("outcome", "predictor", "copredictor", "estimator", "noop", "item_set",
          "cell_weight", "measure", "pred_form")

menu <- readr::read_csv("data/menu_options.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
curve <- readr::read_csv("data/spec_curve.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  datawizard::data_arrange("r_ca") |>
  datawizard::data_modify(idx = seq_along(r_ca) - 1L)
curve_neg <- readr::read_csv("data/spec_curve_negative.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
deviations <- readr::read_csv("data/menu_deviations.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
twin_index <- datawizard::data_select(curve, select = c(axes, "idx"))
pair_rows <- readr::read_csv("data/menu_deviations_rows.csv.gz", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  datawizard::data_filter(curve == "positive" & axis != "se") |>
  dplyr::left_join(twin_index, by = axes)
stopifnot(!anyNA(pair_rows$idx), nrow(curve) == 864)

pairs <- pair_rows |>
  datawizard::data_modify(key = paste(axis, option, rule, sep = "|")) |>
  split(~key) |>
  purrr::map(\(d) list(i = d$idx, r = round(d$r_ca_dev, 4), s = as.integer(d$p_dev < 0.05)))

# the cells and countries left by the two series that do not cover the panel
coverage <- pair_rows |>
  datawizard::data_filter(option %in% c("es_1574_tips", "es_growth")) |>
  dplyr::distinct(option, n_cells_dev, n_countries_dev) |>
  split(~option) |>
  purrr::map(\(d) list(cells = d$n_cells_dev[1], countries = d$n_countries_dev[1]))

curve_js <- curve |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(vary)), idx,
    r_ca = round(r_ca, 4),
    p_conv = signif(p_conv, 3), p_cr1 = signif(p_cr1, 3), p_cr2 = signif(p_cr2, 3),
    ref = is_reference
  )
neg_js <- curve_neg |>
  dplyr::transmute(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(vary)), r_ca = round(r_ca, 4),
                   p_cr2 = signif(p_cr2, 3))

# page titles without their Markdown emphasis, for the links to the teaching pages;
# a path that ends in the id of a section takes the title of its page
pages <- unique(menu$taught_on) |>
  purrr::set_names() |>
  purrr::map(\(f) gsub("*", "", rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(sub("#.*", "", f))$title, fixed = TRUE))

ojs_define(menu_raw = menu, curve_raw = curve_js, neg_raw = neg_js, dev_raw = deviations,
           pairs_raw = pairs, coverage_raw = coverage, pages_raw = pages)
```

The map lays out every decision that an analysis of the claim has to make, in the order in which an analyst meets them on the way from the data to a verdict. Each decision shows all its options, those that are on the curve of 864 specifications and those that the course teaches but has taken off the curve because they answer another question or answer this one less well, and the map opens on the reproduced specification of the course.

Selecting an option rewrites the estimand statement, with the phrases that the choice changed marked, and opens a description of the option: what it estimates, whether it is a justifiable way of answering the claim, what it does to the results when it is swapped into the specifications of the curve, and where in the course it is taught. The sections below the map give the full reasoning and the evidence behind each option.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// Data and constants of the map. This chunk displays nothing: a named cell
// whose value is not a DOM node would otherwise print as an inspector line.
menu = transpose(menu_raw)
curve = transpose(curve_raw)
negCurve = transpose(neg_raw)
devRows = transpose(dev_raw)
VARY = ["outcome", "predictor", "copredictor", "estimator", "noop", "item_set", "cell_weight", "measure", "pred_form"]
ALL_AXES = ["sample", "outcome", "construction", "noop", "item_set", "cell_weight", "predictor", "measure", "pred_form", "estimator", "copredictor", "weights", "family", "se"]
curveKey = d => VARY.map(a => d[a]).join("|")
curveIndex = new Map(curve.map((d, k) => [curveKey(d), k]))
negIndex = new Map(negCurve.map((d, k) => [curveKey(d), k]))

DM = {
  return {
    stages: [
      {id: "data", title: "The data and the sample", note: "Which country-years enter the analysis, and so which population the answer describes.", axes: ["sample"]},
      {id: "outcome", title: "The outcome", note: "How the answers to the question on what the EU means become one number for each country-year.", axes: ["outcome", "construction", "noop", "item_set", "cell_weight"]},
      {id: "predictor", title: "The predictor", note: "Which figure stands for poor national economic performance, and in what form it enters.", axes: ["predictor", "measure", "pred_form"]},
      {id: "comparison", title: "The comparison", note: "Which country-years are compared with which, and what is held fixed while they are compared.", axes: ["estimator", "copredictor"]},
      {id: "average", title: "Whose average", note: "How much each country-year counts in the slope.", axes: ["weights"]},
      {id: "model", title: "The model form", note: "The model that is fitted to the cell means.", axes: ["family"]},
      {id: "inference", title: "The inference", note: "How uncertain the slope is said to be, which decides its class on the curve.", axes: ["se"]}
    ],
    colour: {outcome: "#0e3b6a", construction: "#1f4c7c", predictor: "#2a5d8f", copredictor: "#4a78ab", sample: "#0f6b6b", weights: "#2b8585", estimator: "#8c5a10",
             noop: "#4a7a3f", item_set: "#4a7a3f", cell_weight: "#4a7a3f", measure: "#4a7a3f", pred_form: "#7b6a8f", family: "#7b6a8f", se: "#7b6a8f"},
    levelName: {estimand: "The question", measurement: "Measurement", estimation: "The model"},
    levelShort: {estimand: "Question", measurement: "Measurement", estimation: "Model"},
    judgement: {kept: "On the curve", other_question: "Another question", weaker_answer: "A weaker answer", check: "A check"},
    ruleLabel: {cr2: "CR2 errors with Satterthwaite df", re_conventional: "model-based errors", re_cr1_g1: "errors clustered by country (CR1, 26 df)",
                rewb_satterthwaite: "Satterthwaite df", rewb_cr2: "CR2 errors with Satterthwaite df", beta_cr1_g1: "errors clustered by country (CR1, 26 df)",
                mi_rubin_cr1_g1: "a clustered test pooled over ten imputations (26 df)", conventional: "conventional errors", cr1_g1: "errors clustered by country (CR1, 26 df)",
                identical_to_count: "the test of the count"},
    preferredRule: {re: "re_cr1_g1", rewb: "rewb_cr2", beta: "beta_cr1_g1", mi_mice: "mi_rubin_cr1_g1", mi_amelia: "mi_rubin_cr1_g1"},
    sePcol: {cr2: "p_cr2", cr1: "p_cr1", conventional: "p_conv"},
    seDev: {cr1: "cr1_g1", conventional: "conventional"},
    seName: {cr2: "CR2 errors", cr1: "CR1 errors", conventional: "conventional errors"},
    kItems: {all: {mcosmo: 5, mutil: 2, mcomm: 4, mlib: 2, mpos: 7, mneg: 6}, un: {mcosmo: 5, mutil: 2, mcomm: 3, mlib: 2, mpos: 7, mneg: 5}},
    numWord: {2: "two", 3: "three", 4: "four", 5: "five", 6: "six", 7: "seven"},
    negativeOutcomes: ["mcomm", "mlib", "mneg"],
    domainR: [-0.66, 0.32]
  };
}

// numbers as the site prints them: fixed decimals and a true minus sign
fmtR = x => (x < 0 ? "−" : "") + Math.abs(x).toFixed(3)
// four decimals below 0.001 and within 0.005 of the threshold, so that a p
// just above 0.05 never prints as 0.050
fmtP = p => p < 0.0001 ? "< 0.0001" : p < 0.001 || Math.abs(p - 0.05) < 0.005 ? p.toFixed(4) : p.toFixed(3)
// "p = 0.029" or "p < 0.0001", so that a bound never follows an equals sign
pEq = p => p < 0.0001 ? "p < 0.0001" : `p = ${fmtP(p)}`
fmtPct = x => x.toFixed(1) + "%"
```

::: {.column-page}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
decisionMap = {
  const opt = (axis, code) => menu.find(d => d.axis === axis && d.option === code);
  const optionsOf = axis => menu.filter(d => d.axis === axis);
  const col = axis => DM.colour[axis];
  const el = (tag, attrs, ...kids) => {
    const n = document.createElement(tag);
    if (attrs) for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(attrs)) {
      if (k === "class") n.className = v;
      else if (k === "text") n.textContent = v;
      else if (k === "style") n.setAttribute("style", v);
      else n.setAttribute(k, v);
    }
    for (const kid of kids) if (kid !== null && kid !== undefined) n.append(kid);
    return n;
  };
  // the first ".qmd" of a path, so that the id of a section after it stays in the address
  const pageLink = file => el("a", {href: file.replace(".qmd", ".html")}, pages_raw[file] || file);

  // ---- state: one option per decision, starting from the reproduced specification
  const refRow = curve.find(d => d.ref === true);
  const REF = {sample: "all", weights: "none", construction: "share", family: "gaussian", se: "cr2"};
  for (const a of VARY) REF[a] = refRow[a];
  let sel = Object.assign({}, REF);
  let lastOn = Object.assign({}, REF);
  let lastUnempSeries = REF.measure;
  let latest = null;
  let prevText = null;

  const isOn = (s, a) => opt(a, s[a]).on_curve === true;
  const offAxes = s => ALL_AXES.filter(a => !isOn(s, a));

  // the specification on the curve that stands in for every off-curve choice
  // with the last on-curve option of that decision
  function twinOf(s) {
    const t = Object.assign({}, s);
    for (const a of ALL_AXES) if (!isOn(s, a)) t[a] = lastOn[a];
    if (t.predictor === "growth") { t.measure = "wb_growth"; t.pred_form = "raw"; }
    else if (t.measure === "wb_growth" || t.measure === "es_growth") t.measure = lastUnempSeries;
    return t;
  }
  const curveRowOf = s => { const k = curveIndex.get(curveKey(s)); return k === undefined ? null : curve[k]; };

  function choose(axis, code) {
    const prev = Object.assign({}, sel);
    sel[axis] = code;
    if (axis === "predictor") {
      if (code === "growth") { sel.measure = prev.measure === "es_growth" ? "es_growth" : "wb_growth"; sel.pred_form = "raw"; }
      else if (sel.measure === "wb_growth" || sel.measure === "es_growth") sel.measure = lastUnempSeries;
    }
    if (axis === "measure") {
      const growthSeries = code === "wb_growth" || code === "es_growth";
      sel.predictor = growthSeries ? "growth" : "unemp";
      if (growthSeries) sel.pred_form = "raw";
    }
    for (const a of ALL_AXES) if (isOn(sel, a)) lastOn[a] = sel[a];
    if (sel.predictor === "unemp" && isOn(sel, "measure")) lastUnempSeries = sel.measure;
    latest = axis;
  }

  // ---- the estimand statement, as segments that can be compared with the last one
  function statement(s) {
    const o = a => opt(a, s[a]);
    const k = DM.kItems[s.item_set][s.outcome];
    const outcomeText = o("construction").phrase.replace("{frames}", o("outcome").phrase).replace("{k}", DM.numWord[k]);
    let sampleText = o("sample").phrase;
    if (s.measure === "es_1574_tips") {
      const c = coverage_raw.es_1574_tips;
      sampleText = s.sample === "all"
        ? `the ${c.cells} country-years that the Eurostat table tipsun20 covers, from ${c.countries} member states without the United Kingdom and, before 2009, only France and Sweden`
        : `${sampleText}, and of these only the country-years that the Eurostat table tipsun20 covers`;
    }
    if (s.measure === "es_growth") {
      const c = coverage_raw.es_growth;
      sampleText = s.sample === "all"
        ? `the ${c.cells} country-years of the ${c.countries} member states other than the United Kingdom, which the Eurostat growth series does not cover`
        : `${sampleText}, without the United Kingdom`;
    }
    const other = s.predictor === "unemp" ? "GDP growth" : "the unemployment rate";
    const predName = s.predictor === "unemp" ? "unemployment" : "GDP growth";
    const seg = (key, text, lv, colourAxis) => ({key, text, lv, colourAxis: colourAxis || key});
    return {
      question: [
        "Among ", seg("sample", sampleText, "l1"), ", with ", seg("weights", o("weights").phrase, "l1"),
        ", the association between ", seg("predictor", o("predictor").phrase, "l1"),
        " (", seg("measure", o("measure").phrase, "l2"), ") and ", seg("outcome", outcomeText, "l1"),
        " (", seg("item_set", o("item_set").phrase, "l2"), ", ", seg("noop", o("noop").phrase, "l2"), ", ",
        seg("cell_weight", o("cell_weight").phrase, "l2"), "), comparing ", seg("estimator", o("estimator").phrase, "l1"),
        ", ", seg("copredictor", o("copredictor").phrase.replace("{other}", other), "l1"), "."
      ],
      method: [
        "Answered with ", seg("family", o("family").phrase, "l3"), ", ",
        seg("pred_form", o("pred_form").phrase.replace("{pred}", predName), "l3"), ", and tested by ", seg("se", o("se").phrase, "l3"), "."
      ]
    };
  }
  function renderSegments(target, parts) {
    target.replaceChildren();
    for (const p of parts) {
      if (typeof p === "string") { target.append(p); continue; }
      const span = el("span", {class: `dm-seg ${p.lv}`, style: `--c:${col(p.colourAxis)}`, text: p.text});
      const changed = prevText !== null && prevText[p.key] !== undefined && prevText[p.key] !== p.text;
      target.append(changed ? el("mark", {class: "dm-changed"}, span) : span);
    }
  }

  // ---- what the selection gives
  function pairKey(axis, code) {
    const c = axis === "construction" && code === "rate" ? "count" : code;
    const rule = DM.preferredRule[c] || "cr2";
    const key = `${axis}|${c}|${rule}`;
    return pairs_raw[key] ? {key, rule} : null;
  }
  function verdictOf(s) {
    if (s.family === "beta" && s.construction === "count") return {kind: "inadmissible"};
    const off = offAxes(s).filter(a => a !== "se");
    if (off.length === 0) {
      const d = curveRowOf(s);
      const p = d[DM.sePcol[s.se]];
      return {kind: "curve", d, p, rule: s.se};
    }
    if (off.length === 1 && off[0] === "outcome" && DM.negativeOutcomes.includes(s.outcome)) {
      const k = negIndex.get(curveKey(s));
      return {kind: "negative", d: k === undefined ? null : negCurve[k]};
    }
    if (off.length === 1) {
      const a = off[0], pk = pairKey(a, s[a]);
      const twin = curveRowOf(twinOf(s));
      if (pk === null || twin === null) return {kind: "unfitted", axes: off};
      const P = pairs_raw[pk.key];
      const k = P.i.indexOf(twin.idx);
      if (k < 0) return {kind: "outside", axis: a, twin};
      return {kind: "refit", axis: a, rule: pk.rule, r: P.r[k], sig: P.s[k] === 1, twin};
    }
    return {kind: "unfitted", axes: off};
  }

  // ---- the map
  const stageEls = {};
  const chipEls = [];
  const verdictBox = el("p", {class: "dm-verdict", "aria-live": "polite"});
  const resetBtn = el("button", {type: "button", class: "dm-reset"}, "Back to the reproduced specification");
  const stagesBox = el("div", {class: "dm-stages"});
  DM.stages.forEach((st, si) => {
    const box = el("section", {class: "dm-stage", "aria-labelledby": `dm-stage-${st.id}`},
      el("div", {class: "dm-stage-head"}, el("span", {class: "dm-stage-num", "aria-hidden": "true"}, String(si + 1)),
        el("h3", {id: `dm-stage-${st.id}`}, st.title)),
      el("p", {class: "dm-stage-note"}, st.note));
    for (const axis of st.axes) {
      const opts = optionsOf(axis);
      const first = opts[0];
      const nameId = `dm-dec-${axis}`;
      const group = el("div", {class: "dm-chips", role: "group", "aria-labelledby": nameId});
      for (const o of opts) {
        const tip = o.on_curve ? `${o.label}: on the curve` : `${o.label}: off the curve, taught on ${pages_raw[o.taught_on] || o.taught_on}`;
        const b = el("button", {type: "button", class: "dm-chip" + (o.on_curve ? "" : " off"), style: `--c:${col(axis)}`,
                                "aria-pressed": "false", title: tip, "aria-label": tip, "data-tip": tip}, o.label);
        b.addEventListener("click", () => {
          if (b.getAttribute("aria-disabled") === "true") return;
          const before = b.getBoundingClientRect().top;
          choose(axis, o.option);
          update(st.id);
          const after = b.getBoundingClientRect().top;
          if (Math.abs(after - before) > 1) window.scrollBy(0, after - before);
        });
        chipEls.push({b, axis, code: o.option});
        group.append(b);
      }
      box.append(el("div", {class: "dm-decision"},
        el("div", {class: "dm-decision-name", id: nameId}, first.decision,
          el("span", {class: "lv", style: `color:${col(axis)}`}, DM.levelShort[first.level])),
        group));
    }
    stageEls[st.id] = box;
    stagesBox.append(box);
  });
  const verdictStage = el("section", {class: "dm-stage", "aria-labelledby": "dm-stage-verdict"},
    el("div", {class: "dm-stage-head"}, el("span", {class: "dm-stage-num", "aria-hidden": "true"}, String(DM.stages.length + 1)),
      el("h3", {id: "dm-stage-verdict"}, "The verdict")),
    verdictBox, resetBtn);
  stagesBox.append(verdictStage);
  resetBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const before = resetBtn.getBoundingClientRect().top;
    sel = Object.assign({}, REF); lastOn = Object.assign({}, REF); lastUnempSeries = REF.measure;
    latest = null; update(null);
    const after = resetBtn.getBoundingClientRect().top;
    if (Math.abs(after - before) > 1) window.scrollBy(0, after - before);
  });

  // ---- the panel: statement, the selected option, its twins, the curve
  const statementP = el("p", {class: "dm-statement", "aria-live": "polite"});
  const methodP = el("p", {class: "dm-method"});
  const changedNote = el("p", {class: "dm-small"});
  const optionBox = el("div");
  const pairBox = el("div");
  const curveBox = el("div");
  const panel = el("div", {class: "dm-panel", role: "region", "aria-label": "The selection and its results"},
    el("h3", {}, "The estimand statement"), statementP, methodP, changedNote,
    el("h3", {}, "The selected option"), optionBox,
    el("h3", {}, "Against its twins on the curve"), pairBox,
    el("h3", {}, "The curve of 864"), curveBox);
  const side = el("div", {class: "dm-side"});
  const topSlot = el("div");
  const layout = el("div", {class: "dm-layout"}, el("div", {}, topSlot, stagesBox), side);

  const legend = el("div", {class: "dm-legend"},
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#0e3b6a"}), el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#0f6b6b"}), el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#8c5a10"}), DM.levelName.estimand),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#4a7a3f"}), DM.levelName.measurement),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "sw", style: "background:#7b6a8f"}), DM.levelName.estimation),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "chip-sample"}, "solid"), "on the curve"),
    el("span", {}, el("span", {class: "chip-sample off"}, "dashed"), "in the course, off the curve"));

  const wide = window.matchMedia("(min-width: 1100px)");
  function place(stageId) {
    if (wide.matches) { if (panel.parentNode !== side) side.append(panel); return; }
    if (stageId === null || stageId === undefined) { if (panel.parentNode !== topSlot) topSlot.append(panel); return; }
    const anchor = stageId === "verdict" ? verdictStage : stageEls[stageId];
    if (anchor.nextSibling !== panel) anchor.after(panel);
  }

  // ---- charts
  const recipe = d => VARY.map(a => opt(a, d[a]).label).join("; ");
  function curveChart(width, v) {
    const onAxes = VARY.filter(a => isOn(sel, a));
    const match = curve.filter(d => onAxes.every(a => d[a] === sel[a]));
    const matchSet = new Set(match.map(d => d.idx));
    const showLatest = latest !== null && VARY.includes(latest) && isOn(sel, latest);
    const latestRows = showLatest ? curve.filter(d => d[latest] === sel[latest] && !matchSet.has(d.idx)) : [];
    const latestSet = new Set(latestRows.map(d => d.idx));
    const base = curve.filter(d => !matchSet.has(d.idx) && !latestSet.has(d.idx));
    const x = d => d.idx + 1;
    const dots = (data, stroke, opSig, opNs, r, sw) => [
      Plot.dot(data.filter(d => d.p_cr2 < 0.05), {x, y: "r_ca", r, symbol: "circle", fill: "none", stroke, strokeOpacity: opSig, strokeWidth: sw, title: d => `${recipe(d)}\nr = ${fmtR(d.r_ca)}, CR2 ${pEq(d.p_cr2)}`}),
      Plot.dot(data.filter(d => d.p_cr2 >= 0.05), {x, y: "r_ca", r, symbol: "times", fill: "none", stroke, strokeOpacity: opNs, strokeWidth: sw, title: d => `${recipe(d)}\nr = ${fmtR(d.r_ca)}, CR2 ${pEq(d.p_cr2)}`})
    ];
    const ref = curve.filter(d => d.ref === true);
    const marks = [
      Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#9aa8b3", strokeWidth: 0.8}),
      ...dots(base, "#1d2731", 0.25, 0.12, 3.6, 0.7),
      ...dots(latestRows, col(latest || "outcome"), 0.65, 0.5, 3.6, 0.9),
      ...dots(match, "#8b1538", 1, 1, 5.5, 1.6),
      Plot.text(ref, {x, y: "r_ca", text: () => "reproduced", dy: 16, fontSize: 10, fill: "#1d2731"})
    ];
    if (v.kind === "refit") {
      marks.push(Plot.ruleY([v.r], {stroke: "#8b1538", strokeDasharray: "4,3", strokeWidth: 1}));
      marks.push(Plot.text([v.r], {x: 860, y: d => d, text: () => `refitted: r = ${fmtR(v.r)}`, textAnchor: "end", dy: -6, fontSize: 10, fill: "#8b1538"}));
    }
    return Plot.plot({
      width, height: Math.max(230, Math.min(320, Math.round(width * 0.5))), marginLeft: 46, marginRight: 10, marginBottom: 38,
      style: {fontSize: "11px", background: "transparent"},
      ariaLabel: "The curve of 864 specifications, with the current selection marked",
      x: {domain: [0, 865], label: "864 specifications, ranked by claim-aligned r →", ticks: 4},
      y: {domain: DM.domainR, label: "↑ Claim-aligned partial r", grid: true, ticks: 5},
      marks
    });
  }
  function pairData(axis, code) {
    if (axis === "se") {
      const yCol = DM.sePcol[code];
      const xCol = code === "cr2" ? "p_conv" : "p_cr2";
      return curve.map(d => {
        const xv = Math.max(d[xCol], 1e-4), yv = Math.max(d[yCol], 1e-4);
        const cx = d.r_ca < 0 && d[xCol] < 0.05, cy = d.r_ca < 0 && d[yCol] < 0.05;
        return {x: xv, y: yv, s: d[yCol] < 0.05, changed: cx !== cy, twin: d, label: recipe(d)};
      });
    }
    const pk = pairKey(axis, code);
    if (pk === null) return null;
    const P = pairs_raw[pk.key];
    return P.i.map((ti, k) => {
      const t = curve[ti];
      const twinClass = t.r_ca < 0 && t.p_cr2 < 0.05, devClass = P.r[k] < 0 && P.s[k] === 1;
      return {x: t.r_ca, y: P.r[k], s: P.s[k] === 1, changed: twinClass !== devClass, twin: t, label: recipe(t)};
    });
  }
  function pairChart(width, axis, code, data, isSelPair) {
    const isSe = axis === "se";
    const same = data.filter(d => !d.changed), moved = data.filter(d => d.changed);
    const selPair = data.filter(d => isSelPair(d.twin));
    const c = col(axis);
    const dots = (rows, stroke, op, r, sw) => [
      Plot.dot(rows.filter(d => d.s), {x: "x", y: "y", r, symbol: "circle", fill: "none", stroke, strokeOpacity: op, strokeWidth: sw, title: d => `${d.label}\n${fmtR(d.x)} → ${fmtR(d.y)}`}),
      Plot.dot(rows.filter(d => !d.s), {x: "x", y: "y", r, symbol: "times", fill: "none", stroke, strokeOpacity: op * 0.8, strokeWidth: sw, title: d => `${d.label}\n${fmtR(d.x)} → ${fmtR(d.y)}`})
    ];
    const lo = isSe ? 1e-4 : DM.domainR[0], hi = isSe ? 1 : DM.domainR[1];
    const xName = isSe ? (code === "cr2" ? "p under conventional errors" : "p under CR2, the rule of the curve") : "claim-aligned r on the curve";
    const yName = isSe ? `p under ${DM.seName[code]}` : "claim-aligned r with this option";
    return Plot.plot({
      width, height: Math.max(240, Math.min(360, Math.round(width * 0.62))), marginLeft: 50, marginRight: 12, marginBottom: 40,
      style: {fontSize: "11px", background: "transparent"},
      ariaLabel: `Each specification on the curve set against the same specification with ${opt(axis, code).label}`,
      x: isSe ? {type: "log", domain: [lo, hi], label: `${xName} →`, ticks: 4, tickFormat: "~g"} : {domain: [lo, hi], label: `${xName} →`, ticks: 5},
      y: isSe ? {type: "log", domain: [lo, hi], label: `↑ ${yName}`, ticks: 4, tickFormat: "~g"} : {domain: [lo, hi], label: `↑ ${yName}`, ticks: 5},
      marks: [
        isSe ? Plot.ruleX([0.05], {stroke: "#9aa8b3", strokeDasharray: "3,3"}) : Plot.ruleX([0], {stroke: "#9aa8b3", strokeWidth: 0.8}),
        isSe ? Plot.ruleY([0.05], {stroke: "#9aa8b3", strokeDasharray: "3,3"}) : Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#9aa8b3", strokeWidth: 0.8}),
        Plot.line([[lo, lo], [hi, hi]], {stroke: "#5b6b78", strokeDasharray: "4,3", strokeWidth: 0.8}),
        ...dots(same, "#1d2731", 0.3, 3.4, 0.7),
        ...dots(moved, c, 0.75, 3.4, 0.9),
        ...dots(selPair, "#8b1538", 1, 6, 1.8)
      ]
    });
  }

  // ---- the selected option, in words and numbers
  const curveShares = {
    below: 100 * d3.mean(curve, d => d.r_ca < 0 ? 1 : 0),
    sig: 100 * d3.mean(curve, d => d.r_ca < 0 && d.p_cr2 < 0.05 ? 1 : 0)
  };
  function summaryText(axis, code, o) {
    const negative = axis === "outcome" && DM.negativeOutcomes.includes(code);
    const devCode = axis === "se" ? DM.seDev[code] : code;
    const rows = devRows.filter(d => d.curve === (negative ? "negative" : "positive") && d.axis === axis && d.option === devCode);
    const out = [];
    if (negative) {
      const r = rows[0];
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, `The curve of this claim holds no specification of this scale. On the curve of the negative scales, aligned so that below zero is the direction of the other half of the hypothesis, its 288 specifications lie below zero in ${fmtPct(r.below_zero)} of cases and below zero with CR2 p < 0.05 in ${fmtPct(r.below_zero_sig)}, with a median claim-aligned r of ${fmtR(r.median_r_ca)}.`));
      return out;
    }
    if (axis === "se" && code === "cr2") {
      const conv = 100 * d3.mean(curve, d => d.r_ca < 0 && d.p_conv < 0.05 ? 1 : 0);
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, `Every point of the curve is classed by this rule: ${fmtPct(curveShares.sig)} of the 864 specifications lie below zero with CR2 p < 0.05, against ${fmtPct(conv)} under conventional errors. The partial correlation is the same under every rule, so only the class moves.`));
      return out;
    }
    const withPairs = rows.filter(r => r.n_pairs > 0);
    if (withPairs.length === 0) {
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, code === "wb_growth"
        ? "This is the only growth series on the curve, so there is no other series on the curve to set it against; the Eurostat growth series is compared with it."
        : `Every specification on the curve uses this option, so there is nothing on the curve to set it against; the alternatives on the map are compared with it. On the curve itself ${fmtPct(curveShares.below)} of the 864 specifications lie below zero and ${fmtPct(curveShares.sig)} below zero with CR2 p < 0.05.`));
      return out;
    }
    for (const r of withPairs) {
      const rule = DM.ruleLabel[r.rule] || r.rule;
      const lead = o.on_curve
        ? `Among the ${r.n_pairs} pairs of specifications on the curve that differ only in this decision, the specifications with this option lie below zero in ${fmtPct(r.below_zero)} of cases and below zero with p < 0.05 under ${rule} in ${fmtPct(r.below_zero_sig)}.`
        : `Swapped into the ${r.n_pairs} specifications of the curve to which it applies, this option leaves ${fmtPct(r.below_zero)} of them below zero and ${fmtPct(r.below_zero_sig)} below zero with p < 0.05 under ${rule}, against ${fmtPct(curveShares.sig)} on the curve itself.`;
      const rest = axis === "se"
        ? ` The partial correlations stay as they are, so only the class can move, and it moves for ${fmtPct(r.class_changes)} of the specifications.`
        : ` Their median claim-aligned r is ${fmtR(r.median_r_ca)}, a median shift of ${fmtR(r.median_shift)} from their twins; ${fmtPct(r.sign_changes)} of the pairs change sign and ${fmtPct(r.class_changes)} change class.`;
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, lead + rest));
    }
    if (withPairs.some(r => r.rule !== "cr2" && axis !== "se"))
      out.push(el("p", {class: "dm-small"}, "Part of the change of class comes from the test, because this option is tested by a different rule from the CR2 rule of the curve."));
    return out;
  }

  function renderOption(width, v, twinSel) {
    optionBox.replaceChildren();
    pairBox.replaceChildren();
    if (latest === null) {
      optionBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, "The map opens on the reproduced specification: the cosmopolitan share on World Bank unemployment, compared within countries net of the common yearly changes, with respondents who mention nothing scored zero, all 13 items and cells as interviewed. Select any option on the map to read what it estimates and whether it answers the claim."));
      pairBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, "Once an option is selected, a chart here sets each specification on the curve against the same specification with that option."));
      return;
    }
    const axis = latest, code = sel[axis], o = opt(axis, code), c = col(axis);
    optionBox.append(
      el("p", {class: "dm-option-title"}, `${o.decision}: ${o.label}`),
      el("span", {class: "dm-badge", style: `--c:${c}`}, DM.levelName[o.level]),
      el("span", {class: "dm-badge" + (o.on_curve ? "" : " off"), style: `--c:${o.on_curve ? "#1d2731" : "#8b1538"}`}, DM.judgement[o.judgement]),
      el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, el("b", {}, "What it estimates. "), o.estimates),
      el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, el("b", {}, o.on_curve ? "Why it is on the curve. " : "Why it is off the curve. "), o.explanation),
      el("p", {class: "dm-small"}, "Taught on ", pageLink(o.taught_on), "."));
    for (const p of summaryText(axis, code, o)) pairBox.append(p);
    const data = DM.negativeOutcomes.includes(code) && axis === "outcome" ? null : pairData(axis, code);
    if (data !== null && data.length > 0) {
      const box = el("div", {class: "dm-chart"});
      // the pairs of the selection: twins that match it on every decision but this
      // one (the series and form follow a change of predictor)
      const free = a => a === axis || (axis === "predictor" && (a === "measure" || a === "pred_form"));
      const isSelPair = t => twinSel !== null && VARY.every(a => free(a) || t[a] === twinSel[a]);
      box.append(pairChart(width, axis, code, data, isSelPair));
      pairBox.append(box);
      const label = o.label;
      const caption = axis === "se"
        ? `Each mark is one of the 864 specifications on the curve, placed by its p-value under ${code === "cr2" ? "conventional errors" : "CR2, the rule of the curve"} (horizontal) and under ${DM.seName[code]} (vertical), on logarithmic scales; values below 0.0001 are drawn at 0.0001. The dashed lines mark p = 0.05 and the diagonal marks equal p-values. Circles are significant at 5% on the vertical rule, crosses are not; coloured marks change class (below zero with p < 0.05, or not) between the two rules. The burgundy mark is the specification of the current selection.`
        : `Each mark is one pair: a specification on the curve, placed horizontally by its claim-aligned partial r, and the same specification with ${label}, placed vertically. Marks on the dashed diagonal are unchanged, and marks below it lie further in the direction of the claim. Circles are significant at 5% under the test of the option, crosses are not; coloured marks change class (below zero with p < 0.05, or not) between the two members of the pair. The burgundy mark is the pair of the current selection, where there is one.`;
      pairBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-caption"}, caption));
    }
  }

  function renderVerdict(v) {
    const parts = [];
    const sym = sig => sig ? "an open circle, significant at 5%" : "a cross, not significant at 5%";
    if (v.kind === "curve") {
      const d = v.d, k = d.idx;
      const ruleTxt = v.rule === "cr2" ? "CR2" : DM.seName[v.rule];
      parts.push(`The selection is one of the 864 specifications on the curve: claim-aligned r = ${fmtR(d.r_ca)}, ${ruleTxt} ${pEq(v.p)}.`);
      if (v.rule !== "cr2") parts.push(` The curve classes it by CR2, ${pEq(d.p_cr2)}, which draws it as ${sym(d.p_cr2 < 0.05)}.`);
      else parts.push(` On the curve it is ${sym(d.p_cr2 < 0.05)}.`);
      parts.push(` On the curve, ${fmtPct(100 * k / 864)} of the specifications lie further in the direction of the claim.`);
      if (sel.predictor === "growth") parts.push(" The sign of growth is reversed on the curve, because the claim expects framing to rise with growth.");
      return parts.join("");
    }
    const off = offAxes(sel).filter(a => a !== "se");
    const why = off.map(a => `${opt(a, sel[a]).decision.toLowerCase()} – ${opt(a, sel[a]).label} (${DM.judgement[opt(a, sel[a]).judgement].toLowerCase()})`).join("; ");
    if (v.kind === "inadmissible") return "A count is a number of items, not a proportion, so the beta family cannot model it, and the menu holds no such analysis.";
    let txt = `The curve holds no analysis with this selection, because of ${off.length === 1 ? "one choice" : "these choices"}: ${why}. The burgundy marks are the specifications on the curve that share every other choice.`;
    if (v.kind === "negative" && v.d) txt += ` On the curve of the negative scales this specification has claim-aligned r = ${fmtR(v.d.r_ca)} and CR2 ${pEq(v.d.p_cr2)}, aligned so that below zero is the direction of the other half of the hypothesis.`;
    if (v.kind === "refit") txt += ` Refitted with this option, the closest specification on the curve moves from r = ${fmtR(v.twin.r_ca)} to r = ${fmtR(v.r)}, ${v.sig ? "with p < 0.05" : "with p ≥ 0.05"} under ${DM.ruleLabel[v.rule]}; the dashed line marks where that refit would sit.`;
    if (v.kind === "outside") txt += " This option was fitted only at the standard measurement settings (raw unemployment in the World Bank series, all items, cells as interviewed), and the selection differs from them, so no refit of it exists.";
    if (v.kind === "unfitted" && off.length > 1) txt += " Each option off the curve was fitted one at a time against the curve, so this combination of options was never fitted.";
    return txt;
  }

  let lastWidth = 0;
  function drawPanel() {
    const width = Math.max(280, Math.floor(panel.clientWidth - 34));
    lastWidth = width;
    const v = verdictOf(sel);
    const twin = curveRowOf(offAxes(sel).filter(a => a !== "se").length === 0 ? sel : twinOf(sel));
    renderOption(width, v, twin);
    curveBox.replaceChildren();
    const box = el("div", {class: "dm-chart"});
    box.append(curveChart(width, v));
    curveBox.append(el("p", {class: "dm-text"}, renderVerdict(v)), box,
      el("p", {class: "dm-caption"}, `Each mark is one of the 864 specifications on the curve of the claim, ranked by its claim-aligned partial r, where below zero is the direction of the claim. Open circles are significant at 5% under CR2 errors clustered by country, crosses are not. Burgundy marks are the specifications that match every on-curve choice of the selection${latest !== null && VARY.includes(latest) && isOn(sel, latest) ? `, and the coloured marks are the other specifications that share the option selected last (${opt(latest, sel[latest]).label})` : ""}. The ink label marks the reproduced specification.`));
  }

  function update(stageId) {
    for (const {b, axis, code} of chipEls) {
      b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", sel[axis] === code ? "true" : "false");
      const disabled = axis === "pred_form" && code === "log" && sel.predictor === "growth";
      b.setAttribute("aria-disabled", disabled ? "true" : "false");
      const tip = disabled ? "Logged: growth takes negative values, so it enters raw only" : b.getAttribute("data-tip");
      b.title = tip;
      b.setAttribute("aria-label", tip);
    }
    const st = statement(sel);
    renderSegments(statementP, st.question);
    renderSegments(methodP, st.method);
    const nowText = {};
    for (const p of [...st.question, ...st.method]) if (typeof p !== "string") nowText[p.key] = p.text;
    const anyChanged = prevText !== null && Object.keys(nowText).some(k => prevText[k] !== nowText[k]);
    changedNote.textContent = anyChanged
      ? "The marked phrases are the ones that the latest choice changed. Bold phrases state the question, green phrases say how its variables are measured, and the second sentence says how the answer is reached."
      : "Bold phrases state the question, green phrases say how its variables are measured, and the second sentence says how the answer is reached.";
    prevText = nowText;
    const v = verdictOf(sel);
    verdictBox.textContent = v.kind === "curve"
      ? `On the curve: r = ${fmtR(v.d.r_ca)}, ${v.rule === "cr2" ? "CR2" : DM.seName[v.rule]} ${pEq(v.p)}${v.rule === "cr2" ? "" : ` (CR2 ${pEq(v.d.p_cr2)})`}.`
      : v.kind === "refit" ? `Off the curve. Refitted with this option: r = ${fmtR(v.r)}, ${v.sig ? "p < 0.05" : "p ≥ 0.05"} under ${DM.ruleLabel[v.rule]}.`
      : "Off the curve: the course holds no fitted analysis for this combination.";
    place(stageId);
    drawPanel();
  }

  const root = el("div", {class: "dm"}, legend, layout);
  update(null);
  const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => {
    const w = Math.floor(panel.clientWidth - 34);
    if (w > 0 && Math.abs(w - lastWidth) > 24) { place(latest === null ? null : (DM.stages.find(s => s.axes.includes(latest)) || {}).id); drawPanel(); }
  });
  ro.observe(root);
  const onMedia = () => { place(latest === null ? null : (DM.stages.find(s => s.axes.includes(latest)) || {}).id); drawPanel(); };
  wide.addEventListener("change", onMedia);
  invalidation.then(() => { ro.disconnect(); wide.removeEventListener("change", onMedia); });
  return root;
}
```

:::

The three groups of the map are those of the [menu](#level-estimand) below. The two measurement choices that reach into the question as well, the rule for respondents who mention nothing and a published series that covers only part of the panel, are marked in the estimand statement at the moment that they are selected.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# This chunk follows the chunk of the decision map, which sorts curve by the
# claim-aligned r; it reads the curve again, in the order of the file, for the
# sections below.
axes <- c("outcome", "predictor", "copredictor", "estimator", "sample", "weights",
          "construction", "noop", "item_set", "cell_weight", "measure", "pred_form", "family")

curve <- readr::read_csv("data/spec_curve.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
forks <- readr::read_csv("data/spec_curve_forks.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  datawizard::data_filter(curve == "positive")
deviations <- readr::read_csv("data/menu_deviations.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ref <- datawizard::data_filter(curve, is_reference)
# every option swapped into the reproduced specification, read from the pairs file
ref_rows <- readr::read_csv("data/menu_deviations_rows.csv.gz", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  datawizard::data_filter(curve == "positive") |>
  dplyr::semi_join(ref, by = axes)
bw <- readr::read_csv("data/display_between_within.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
inference <- readr::read_csv("data/display_inference.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
means <- readr::read_csv("data/display_country_means.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
pw <- readr::read_csv("data/teney_panel_weights.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# fixed decimals and a true minus sign; percentages round halves up, as the
# decision map does, so that the map and the text print the same figures
num <- \(x, d = 3) sub("^-", "−", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d))
pct <- \(x, d = 1) paste0(formatC(floor(x * 10^d + 0.5) / 10^d, format = "f", digits = d), "%")
pe <- \(p) if (p < 0.0001) "p < 0.0001" else paste("p =", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = if (p < 0.001) 4 else 3))

# shares of a set of curve rows below zero, and below zero with CR2 p < 0.05
below <- \(d) 100 * mean(d$r_ca < 0)
sig <- \(d) 100 * mean(d$r_ca < 0 & d$p_cr2 < 0.05)
sig_rule <- \(col) 100 * mean(curve$r_ca < 0 & curve[[col]] < 0.05)

# one value from the fork table, the option table or the reproduced specification;
# the filters inside these functions are those of dplyr, whose !! tells the
# arguments option and rule apart from the columns of the same names
fk <- \(axis, col = "share") forks[[col]][forks$axis == axis]
dv <- \(option, col, rule = NULL, which = "positive") {
  d <- dplyr::filter(deviations, curve == which, option == !!option)
  if (!is.null(rule)) d <- dplyr::filter(d, rule == !!rule)
  d[[col]][1]
}
rd <- \(option, col, rule = NULL) {
  d <- dplyr::filter(ref_rows, option == !!option)
  if (!is.null(rule)) d <- dplyr::filter(d, rule == !!rule)
  d[[col]][1]
}
bwv <- \(outcome, predictor, col) bw[[col]][bw$outcome == outcome & bw$predictor == predictor]
inf <- \(est, rule, col) inference[[col]][inference$estimator == est & inference$inference == rule]

# the questions fixed by the four decisions about the question that vary on the curve, and
# whether the measurement decisions and the form split each one across classes
questions <- curve |>
  datawizard::data_modify(cls = r_ca < 0 & p_cr2 < 0.05) |>
  dplyr::summarise(straddle = any(cls) & !all(cls),
                   .by = c(outcome, predictor, copredictor, estimator))
twoway <- datawizard::data_filter(curve, estimator == "fe_twoway")
country <- datawizard::data_filter(curve, estimator == "fe_country")
```

## The estimand statement

Write the statement that your analysis will complete:

> Among **which country-years**, with **each counting how much**, the association between **poor economic performance**, measured as **X**, and **positive EU framing**, measured as **Y**, comparing **what with what**, **holding what fixed**.

One question sorts the decisions: would two analysts who chose differently accept each other's number as an answer to the same question? If they would not, the decision belongs to the question, and moving it rewrites a bold slot of the statement other than the two "measured as" slots. If they would, a decision about how a named construct becomes a column of numbers is a measurement decision and changes only a "measured as" slot, and any other decision belongs to the model and leaves the statement as it is, since the statement names what is estimated and says nothing about how the model is fitted or tested. The completed statement is your estimand [@LundbergEtAl2021WhatYourEstimand], and it is what a reader has to know before your coefficient means anything.

The statement is written at the resolution of the claim, which names the constructs and the comparison and not the figures that stand for them, so the choice among published series of unemployment is a measurement decision. The scoring rule, whether the answers of a respondent enter as a share of their own mentions or as a count of the items in the set, looks like one too, since both are built from the same thirteen items. It belongs to the question, because a share and a count remain different quantities however well the items were measured, one the weight of a framing among the frames that a person holds and the other its volume, and two analysts who differ on the rule would not accept each other's number as an estimate of the same thing.

Two measurement decisions reach into the question as well, and both are easy to miss. Scoring respondents who mention nothing as zero keeps every respondent in the cell mean, but the mean then equals the share among those who answered multiplied by the proportion who answered, so that the outcome mixes how people frame the EU with whether they name any meaning of it at all. And a published series that covers only part of the panel is chosen as a measure of the predictor, yet it changes the population of the question as well, since the country-years that the series does not cover drop out of the analysis, and the decision map marks both changes in the statement at the moment that they are made.

The group of a decision also says what kind of reason justifies it. A decision about the question needs an argument from the claim, since it chooses the question: which framing the claim is about, which measure of the economy, which comparison and which population. A measurement decision needs an argument from the instrument and the data, and a decision about the model an argument from the structure of the data, such as the bounds of a share or the correlation of a country with itself over time. An option off the curve can still be the right choice for a different question, and a reason of the right kind will usually say which question that is.

## The curve of 864 {#the-curve}

The curve crosses, for each of the three positive scales scored as shares, the options that answer the claim: unemployment in four published series and in two forms, or GDP growth in the World Bank series; with or without the other economic measure held fixed; two-way or country fixed effects; respondents who mention nothing scored zero or left out; all 13 items or the 12 without "unemployment"; and cells as interviewed or weighted. That gives 256 unemployment and 32 growth specifications for each scale, 288 per scale and 864 in all. Four decisions take a single option on the curve: all 270 country-years, no regression weight, the share as the scoring rule, and a linear model.

Every point is placed by its descriptive partial correlation, aligned with the claim so that below zero is the direction that the claim predicts, and classed by errors clustered by country with the CR2 correction and Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, which allow for the correlation of the residuals of a country from year to year and for the few countries that carry most of the variation. Of the `r nrow(curve)` specifications, `r pct(below(curve))` lie below zero and `r pct(sig(curve))` lie below zero with CR2 p < 0.05; the partial correlations run from `r num(min(curve$r_ca))` to `r num(max(curve$r_ca))`, with a median of `r num(median(curve$r_ca))`. The reproduced specification, the cosmopolitan share on World Bank unemployment under two-way fixed effects with respondents who mention nothing scored zero, gives b = `r num(ref$b, 5)`, t = `r num(ref$t)` on `r ref$df` df and r = `r num(ref$r)`, the value that the reproduction task targets, and its CR2 p-value is `r num(ref$p_cr2, 4)`, on `r num(ref$df_cr2, 1)` Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, just above the threshold of 5%.

Almost every specification on the curve points in the direction of the claim, so the uncertainty that remains concerns the strength of the evidence rather than its direction, and it is divided mainly by two decisions. Under country fixed effects `r pct(sig(country))` of the specifications lie below zero with CR2 p < 0.05, against `r pct(sig(twoway))` under two-way fixed effects; with unemployment as the predictor the shares are `r pct(sig(datawizard::data_filter(country, predictor == "unemp")))` and `r pct(sig(datawizard::data_filter(twoway, predictor == "unemp")))`, while with growth they are `r pct(sig(datawizard::data_filter(curve, predictor == "growth")))` under both designs. @tbl-forks gives, for every decision that varies on the curve, the share of the variance that it carries and how often moving it alone changes the class of a specification.

| Decision | Group | Share of the variance | Class changes when moved alone |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| Estimator | Question | `r pct(fk("estimator"))` | `r pct(fk("estimator", "crossing_rate"))` |
| Predictor | Question | `r pct(fk("predictor"))` | `r pct(fk("predictor", "crossing_rate"))` |
| Frame set | Question | `r pct(fk("outcome"))` | `r pct(fk("outcome", "crossing_rate"))` |
| Adjustment set | Question | `r pct(fk("copredictor"))` | `r pct(fk("copredictor", "crossing_rate"))` |
| Item set | Measurement | `r pct(fk("item_set"))` | `r pct(fk("item_set", "crossing_rate"))` |
| Respondents who mention nothing | Measurement | `r pct(fk("noop"))` | `r pct(fk("noop", "crossing_rate"))` |
| Published series | Measurement | `r pct(fk("measure"))` | `r pct(fk("measure", "crossing_rate"))` |
| Cell weighting | Measurement | `r pct(fk("cell_weight"))` | `r pct(fk("cell_weight", "crossing_rate"))` |
| Predictor form | Model | `r pct(fk("pred_form"))` | `r pct(fk("pred_form", "crossing_rate"))` |
| Interactions | – | `r pct(fk("interactions"))` | – |

: The decisions that vary on the curve of 864. The share of the variance is the share of the variance of the claim-aligned partial r that the decision carries as a main effect; the class changes are the share of pairs of specifications, differing only in that decision, whose members fall in different classes (below zero with CR2 p < 0.05, or not). The predictor pairs raw World Bank unemployment with World Bank growth. Source: `data/spec_curve_forks.csv`. {#tbl-forks}

The numbers on this page are computed from the files that the course pipeline writes to `data/`, the curve in `data/spec_curve.csv` and the comparison of every option with its twins on the curve in `data/menu_deviations.csv`, and `data/menu_options.csv` holds, for every option, the status and the one-sentence reason that the helpers of the browser lab and of the workspace print when the option is off the curve.

## The question {#level-estimand}

Each of these decisions rewrites the estimand statement, so that two analysts who make it differently are answering different questions.

| Decision | On the curve | Off the curve, and where it is taught | Share of the variance | Class changes |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| **Frame set** | cosmopolitan `mcosmo`, utilitarian `mutil`, positive composite `mpos` | communitarian `mcomm`, libertarian `mlib`, negative composite `mneg`, on a curve of their own | `r pct(fk("outcome"))` | `r pct(fk("outcome", "crossing_rate"))` |
| **Scoring rule** | share of mentions `share` | count of items `count`, count per item `rate`, on [The items behind the scales](companion/measurement.qmd) | fixed | – |
| **Predictor** | unemployment `unemp`, GDP growth `growth` | – | `r pct(fk("predictor"))` | `r pct(fk("predictor", "crossing_rate"))` |
| **Adjustment set** | none `none`, the other measure `other` | – | `r pct(fk("copredictor"))` | `r pct(fk("copredictor", "crossing_rate"))` |
| **Sample** | all 270 country-years `all` | 2004–2008 `y2004_2008`, 2009–2013 `y2009_2013`, without the bailout countries `no_bailout`, without Greece and Spain `no_GR_ES`, on [The multiverse and its critics](companion/multiverse.qmd) | fixed | – |
| **Whose average** | each country-year once `none` | respondents `n_cell`, effective sample size `n_eff`, adult population `pop`, in [Whose average](#whose-average) | fixed | – |
| **Estimator** | two-way fixed effects `fe_twoway`, country fixed effects `fe_country` | random effects `re`, pooled OLS `pooled_cl`, within–between model `rewb`, in [the module on panel data](companion/panel-data.qmd#sec-re) | `r pct(fk("estimator"))` | `r pct(fk("estimator", "crossing_rate"))` |

: The seven decisions about the question. The last two columns describe the curve, as in @tbl-forks; "fixed" marks a decision with a single option on the curve. {#tbl-level1}

### Frame set

OA groups the thirteen answer options of the question on what the EU means to the respondent into four dimensions, which cross the valence of a meaning with its content: cosmopolitan (positive and non-materialist), utilitarian (positive and materialist), communitarian (negative and non-materialist) and libertarian (negative and materialist), with a positive and a negative composite built from the two pairs. The claim names the positive dimensions, so the cosmopolitan scale, the utilitarian scale and the positive composite are its outcomes. The composite is the plainest reading of "positive EU-framing dimensions", the cosmopolitan scale is the one that the instruction for the second task of the robustness study of SCORE [Multi100\; @AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness] asked the analysts to use, and the utilitarian scale is the materialist dimension, on which the first hypothesis expects the stronger effect. On the curve the three give `r pct(sig(datawizard::data_filter(curve, outcome == "mcosmo")))`, `r pct(sig(datawizard::data_filter(curve, outcome == "mutil")))` and `r pct(sig(datawizard::data_filter(curve, outcome == "mpos")))` of specifications below zero with CR2 p < 0.05, and the frame set carries `r pct(fk("outcome"))` of the variance on the curve.

The three negative scales answer the other half of the first hypothesis, an increase in negative framing, and they have a curve of their own, `data/spec_curve_negative.csv`, aligned so that below zero is the direction of that half. They are not independent evidence for the claim. Under the share rule the four scales of a respondent sum to one, and when respondents who mention nothing are scored zero, the positive and the negative composites of every country-year add up to one minus the share of respondents who mention nothing; within countries the aligned negative composite and the positive composite correlate at 0.93, so a 'confirmation' on the negative composite largely counts the positive result a second time. The communitarian scale also contains the item "unemployment", which ties the outcome to the predictor by content: removing the item cuts its aligned correlation at the reproduced specification from −0.495 to −0.290. The libertarian scale, finally, shows almost no association, and on the negative curve only `r pct(dv("mlib", "below_zero_sig", which = "negative"))` of its specifications lie below zero with CR2 p < 0.05, against `r pct(dv("mcomm", "below_zero_sig", which = "negative"))` for the communitarian scale and `r pct(dv("mneg", "below_zero_sig", which = "negative"))` for the negative composite. How the thirteen items hang together is examined on [The items behind the scales](companion/measurement.qmd).

### Scoring rule

The scoring rule decides what "more" of a framing means. The share, the measure of the paper, divides the items of a scale that a respondent mentions by all the items that the respondent mentions, so it is a relative frequency: whatever else a respondent mentions lowers the share of every scale. The count is the number of the items of the scale that a respondent mentions, whatever else they mention, and the rate divides the count by the number of items in the scale, so that a two-item and a five-item scale stand on one footing. The claim concerns how citizens frame the EU, which is a matter of composition, and the share is the only rule on the curve.

The count measures something else, the volume of what people say about the EU. Across the country-years the cosmopolitan count correlates `r num(cor(pw$c_mcosmo, pw$mean_items), 2)` with the mean number of items that respondents mention, against `r num(cor(pw$w_mcosmo, pw$mean_items), 2)` for the share, and the two constructions of the cosmopolitan outcome correlate only `r num(cor(pw$w_mcosmo, pw$c_mcosmo), 2)`. A count therefore answers a neighbouring question, whether people say more or fewer positive things about the EU, and it is the construct that KEVF1 and 018OL used, which matters for reading their results. Swapped into the specifications of the curve, the count leaves `r pct(dv("count", "below_zero_sig"))` of them below zero with CR2 p < 0.05, against `r pct(sig(curve))` on the curve, and at the reproduced specification it moves the aligned correlation from `r num(ref$r_ca)` to `r num(rd("count", "r_ca_dev"))` (CR2 `r pe(rd("count", "p_dev"))`). The rate gives exactly the same test and partial correlation as the count in a linear model, since it divides the count by a constant; it is the form of the count that a beta regression can take.

### Predictor

The claim names "poor economic performances", and the paper models two measures of it, the national unemployment rate and annual GDP growth, both of which are justifiable readings and both of which stay on the curve. Unemployment is also the measure that the instruction for the second task of the robustness study named. Growth carries less information within countries, because 59% of its variation within countries is common to all of them in the same year, above all the recession of 2009, which the year effects of the two-way design remove. Its slope within countries on the cosmopolitan scale is small (`r num(bwv("mcosmo", "growth", "b_within"), 5)`, CR2 `r pe(bwv("mcosmo", "growth", "p_within_cr2"))`), while across the 27 country means the association is clear (`r num(bwv("mcosmo", "growth", "b_between"), 4)`, `r pe(bwv("mcosmo", "growth", "p_between"))`). The claim expects framing to rise with growth, so the sign of every growth specification is reversed on the curve. Moving from unemployment to growth, with everything else fixed, changes the class of `r pct(fk("predictor", "crossing_rate"))` of the pairs, and growth specifications lie below zero with CR2 p < 0.05 in `r pct(sig(datawizard::data_filter(curve, predictor == "growth")))` of cases, against `r pct(sig(datawizard::data_filter(curve, predictor == "unemp")))` for unemployment.

### Adjustment set

With unemployment as the predictor, leaving growth out gives the association of framing with unemployment whatever happened to output, and holding growth fixed gives the association at a given rate of growth; with growth as the predictor the roles swap. Neither measure is a confounder of the other in the usual sense, since both are expressions of the same crisis, so the two options are two estimands rather than a right and a wrong set of controls, and both stay on the curve. The unadjusted slope is the one that the reproduced specification estimates, and the adjusted one follows the model of the original study, which carries both measures. Under the principle that the controls which define an estimand belong in every model of it [@YoungCumberworth2025MultiverseAnalysisComputational], the two are better kept as two estimands, each with its own definition, than mixed as interchangeable variants of one. Whether growth is a common cause, a second expression of the downturn or a step on the path from the crisis to framing is a question for the [causal graph](companion/dags.qmd). On the curve the decision carries `r pct(fk("copredictor"))` of the variance and changes the class of `r pct(fk("copredictor", "crossing_rate"))` of the pairs.

### Sample

The population of the claim is the 27 member states over 2004–2013, the 270 country-years of the panel, and it is the only sample on the curve. Each of the four restrictions on the menu answers a question about a different population, which is why the sample is a decision about the question, and none of them is a second way of answering the claim as written. The restrictions are conventionally run as robustness checks, but a check that changes the population changes the estimand statement, and its result cannot confirm or undermine an answer about another population.

- **2004–2008** keeps only the years before the crisis reached most labour markets. A window that contains no crisis cannot speak to whether the crisis undermined positive framing; within countries it measures how framing tracked the smaller fluctuations of those years.
- **2009–2013** keeps only the crisis years, so it drops the comparison with the period before them and asks how framing moved with the deepening and easing of the crisis once it had begun.
- **Without the bailout countries** removes the eight countries that received financial assistance (Cyprus, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Latvia, Portugal, Romania and Spain), in which the crisis was deepest and which carry most of the variation in unemployment that identifies the slope. The question becomes whether the association holds in the countries in which the crisis was mild.
- **Without Greece and Spain** is an influence diagnostic, a check on how much the result owes to the two countries with the largest rises in unemployment, of the kind that @Auspurg2025RobustnessBetterAssessed lists among the forms of nonequivalence as unstable country subsets. A single hand-picked exclusion is a weak form of the diagnostic, which leaving out one country at a time does more completely.

Splitting the panel at 2008 is one rung of a ladder of ways to handle the crisis years, from pooling them with the other years, as the full panel does, through a crisis indicator or a split into periods, to absorbing every year with its own effect, as the two-way design does.

Swapped into the specifications of the curve, the four restrictions leave `r pct(dv("y2004_2008", "below_zero_sig"))` (2004–2008), `r pct(dv("y2009_2013", "below_zero_sig"))` (2009–2013), `r pct(dv("no_bailout", "below_zero_sig"))` (without the bailout countries) and `r pct(dv("no_GR_ES", "below_zero_sig"))` (without Greece and Spain) below zero with CR2 p < 0.05, against `r pct(sig(curve))` on the curve, and the sign changes in `r pct(dv("no_bailout", "sign_changes"))` of the pairs without the bailout countries. The findings that the restrictions carry are kept in three displays on [The multiverse and its critics](companion/multiverse.qmd#sec-heterogeneity), the slope by period, the slope with one country left out at a time and the bailout countries against the rest, so that the curve keeps a single population.

### Whose average

Unweighted, every country-year counts once and the slope describes the average member state, which matches a claim about how national economies shape the framing of their citizens. Malta then counts as much as Germany. Weighting by the number of respondents in a country-year (`n_cell`) or by their effective number, discounted for the unevenness of the survey weights (`n_eff`), is a precision argument: if the cell means differed only in how precisely they are measured, weighting by sample size would estimate the same quantity more efficiently. Weighting by adult population (`pop`) changes the quantity to the average European, in which the largest member state counts `r num(max(pw$pop_15plus) / min(pw$pop_15plus), 0)` times as much as the smallest.

Only the unweighted fit stays on the curve. The precision argument fails on these data, because sampling error is a small part of the variation between country-years, about 7% of what the reproduced model leaves unexplained, so that efficient weights are close to equal and the respondent weights mostly shift weight towards the years with two survey waves and towards the countries with the largest samples; the population weight answers a defensible but different question, which the claim does not ask. Swapped into the specifications of the curve, the respondent weight leaves `r pct(dv("n_cell", "below_zero_sig"))` below zero with CR2 p < 0.05, the effective sample size `r pct(dv("n_eff", "below_zero_sig"))` and the population weight `r pct(dv("pop", "below_zero_sig"))`, which changes the class of `r pct(dv("pop", "class_changes"))` of the pairs.

### Estimator

The estimator decides which country-years are compared with which, and it is the decision that moves results most on the curve, with `r pct(fk("estimator"))` of the variance. Two fixed-effects designs stay on it, as two estimands. Two-way fixed effects removes the stable differences between countries and whatever all member states went through together in a year, so the slope compares each country with itself, relative to the common European path. Country fixed effects keeps the changes that were common to Europe in a given year, which on this panel make up 29% of the variation in unemployment within countries, so its comparison includes the common path; its slope is larger, and it is open to confounding by any shift in framing across Europe that coincided with the crisis. At the reproduced specification the two give r = `r num(inf("fe_twoway", "conventional", "r_descriptive"))` (CR2 p = `r num(inf("fe_twoway", "cr2_satterthwaite", "p"), 4)`) and r = `r num(inf("fe_country", "conventional", "r_descriptive"))` (CR2 `r pe(inf("fe_country", "cr2_satterthwaite", "p"))`), and across the curve moving between them changes the class of `r pct(fk("estimator", "crossing_rate"))` of the pairs. Year effects are the last rung of the ladder that is described under the sample.

**Pooled OLS** regresses framing on unemployment across all 270 country-years at once, so its slope mixes the stable differences between countries with the changes within them, two associations that on these data run in opposite directions, as [the module on panel data](companion/panel-data.qmd#sec-pooled) shows; a pooled slope therefore answers neither the within-country reading of the claim nor the cross-national one. Swapped into the specifications of the curve, pooled OLS leaves `r pct(dv("pooled_cl", "below_zero"))` of them below zero and `r pct(dv("pooled_cl", "below_zero_sig"))` below zero with CR2 p < 0.05, and the sign changes in `r pct(dv("pooled_cl", "sign_changes"))` of the pairs, which is how a different quantity behaves rather than a noisy version of the same one.

**Random effects** fits one slope that is a weighted blend of the within-country and the between-country associations, and it is consistent only if the stable differences between countries are unrelated to the predictor. That assumption fails here: on the course panel the within and the between slopes have opposite signs in `r sum(sign(bw$b_within) != sign(bw$b_between))` of the `r nrow(bw)` combinations of positive scale and predictor, and the test of their difference rejects at the 5% level in `r sum(bw$p_difference < 0.05)` of them, as [the module on panel data](companion/panel-data.qmd#sec-random-effects) sets out. Swapped into the specifications of the curve, the estimator leaves `r pct(dv("re", "below_zero_sig", "re_cr1_g1"))` below zero with p < 0.05 under errors clustered by country, a figure that owes as much to the comparison it makes as to the evidence.

**The within–between model** of @BellJones2015ExplainingFixedEffects separates what random effects blend, the deviation of the predictor from its country mean carrying the within slope and the country mean the between slope. Its within slope equals the fixed-effects slope exactly, so on the curve it would repeat existing points with other errors; its place is in [the module on panel data](companion/panel-data.qmd#sec-within-between), where it shows the two associations side by side, and for the cosmopolitan scale the test of their difference gives `r pe(bwv("mcosmo", "unemp", "p_difference"))`.

## Measurement {#level-measurement}

The question stays fixed, and these decisions change how a named construct becomes a column of numbers.

| Decision | On the curve | Off the curve, and where it is taught | Share of the variance | Class changes |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| **Respondents who mention nothing** | scored zero `zero`, left out `drop` | split rule `split`; multiple imputation `mi_mice`, `mi_amelia`, on [The items behind the scales](companion/measurement.qmd#sec-noop) | `r pct(fk("noop"))` | `r pct(fk("noop", "crossing_rate"))` |
| **Item set** | all 13 items `all`, without "unemployment" `un` | – | `r pct(fk("item_set"))` | `r pct(fk("item_set", "crossing_rate"))` |
| **Cell weighting** | as interviewed `unweighted`, weighted `design` | – | `r pct(fk("cell_weight"))` | `r pct(fk("cell_weight", "crossing_rate"))` |
| **Published series** | unemployment: World Bank `wb_nat`, Eurostat 15–74 `es_1574_act`, Eurostat 20–64 as a share of the population `es_2064_pop`, Labour Force Survey 25–64 `es_2564_lfs`; growth: World Bank `wb_growth` | Eurostat table tipsun20 `es_1574_tips`, Eurostat growth `es_growth`, on [Social science data sources](companion/data-sources.qmd) | `r pct(fk("measure"))` | `r pct(fk("measure", "crossing_rate"))` |

: The four measurement decisions, with the last two columns as in @tbl-forks. {#tbl-level2}

### Respondents who mention nothing

Of all respondents, `r pct(100 * sum(pw$n_noop) / sum(pw$n_cy))` mention none of the 13 items, and under the share rule they have no share at all, so something has to be decided about them. Scoring them zero is the rule of the course panel and of the reproduced specification, and it keeps every respondent; but it changes the construct, since the cell mean then equals the share among those who answered multiplied by the proportion who answered, so that the rate of saying nothing enters every scale. Leaving them out is consistent with the share as a measure, since a respondent with no mentions has no share, and it is what the code of the original study did; its cost is that it conditions on answering. Within countries the rate of saying nothing falls slightly as unemployment rises (b = −0.0011 per point; t = −1.25 with errors clustered by country), so the zero rule pulls the slopes a little towards zero. Both rules stay on the curve, where the drop rule gives `r pct(sig(datawizard::data_filter(curve, noop == "drop")))` of specifications below zero with CR2 p < 0.05 and the zero rule `r pct(sig(datawizard::data_filter(curve, noop == "zero")))`.

The split rule, which leaves out those who said "don't know" or gave no answer and scores off-list answers as zero, has a construct no clearer than that of either rule on the curve, and its results lie close to theirs (`r pct(dv("split", "below_zero_sig"))` below zero with CR2 p < 0.05); the two imputation rules fill in the shares of the silent respondents under a missing-at-random assumption, and since they were computed only at the standard measurement settings they cannot be crossed with the rest of the menu. The section [Respondents who mention nothing](companion/measurement.qmd#sec-noop) of the module on the items behind the scales sets out what each rule assumes about the people who stayed silent.

### Item set

OA builds every scale from the 13 items of the paper, and the code of the original study also builds a second version without the item "unemployment", which leaves the communitarian scale and every denominator one item shorter. When more people name "unemployment" as a meaning of the EU, every other share falls mechanically, so part of a decline in positive shares can be the rise of that one item rather than a change in how positively the EU is framed. Both sets stay on the curve, and the shift between them is the part of the result that the overlap carries: with all items `r pct(sig(datawizard::data_filter(curve, item_set == "all")))` of specifications lie below zero with CR2 p < 0.05, and without "unemployment" `r pct(sig(datawizard::data_filter(curve, item_set == "un")))`. Under the reduced set a respondent whose only mention was "unemployment" has nothing left and joins the respondents who mention nothing.

### Cell weighting

The cell mean can be the mean of the respondents as interviewed, as in the original study and the course panel, or the mean under the post-stratification weight supplied by GESIS, which estimates the mean of the national population. The weighted mean is the better estimator of a national quantity in principle, but the design effects are small, and the decision carries `r pct(fk("cell_weight"), 2)` of the variance on the curve and changes the class of `r pct(fk("cell_weight", "crossing_rate"))` of the pairs. Both options stay on the curve; if a leaner menu were wanted, this would be the first decision to fix.

### Published series

The five analysts merged five different unemployment series, which differ in age band and denominator. The four that cover all 270 country-years move together within countries, correlating between 0.995 and 0.999 once country and year means are removed, and all four stay on the curve, where the decision carries `r pct(fk("measure"))` of the variance. The Eurostat table tipsun20, which KEVF1 merged, is a different matter: it has no row for the United Kingdom and, before 2009, rows only for France and Sweden, so choosing it leaves `r rd("es_1574_tips", "n_cells_dev")` of the 270 country-years. That is a decision about the sample presented as a decision about the measure, and its results describe another population and another period; swapped into the unemployment specifications of the curve, it leaves `r pct(dv("es_1574_tips", "below_zero_sig"))` of them below zero with CR2 p < 0.05, a figure that probably reflects the crisis years, which make up most of its cells, more than the series itself. The Eurostat growth series has no row for the United Kingdom either, so it removes a country from the population, and only the World Bank growth series stays on the curve.

## The model {#level-estimation}

With the question and the measures fixed, these decisions change the model that is fitted and how sure its answer is said to be. Two of the three concern the fit and can move the estimate; the third concerns the inference and moves only the class.

| Decision | On the curve | Off the curve, and where it is taught | Share of the variance | Class changes |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| **Predictor form** | raw `raw`, logged `log` (unemployment only) | – | `r pct(fk("pred_form"), 2)` | `r pct(fk("pred_form", "crossing_rate"))` |
| **Outcome family** | linear `gaussian` | beta regression `beta`, in [Outcome family](#outcome-family) | fixed | – |
| **Inference** | CR2 with Satterthwaite df `cr2` | clustered, CR1 `cr1`, conventional `conventional`, in [the module on panel data](companion/panel-data.qmd#sec-inference) | nil | – |

: The three decisions about the model: two about the fit, one about the inference. The inference cannot change the partial correlation, so its share of the variance is nil. {#tbl-level3}

### Predictor form

Unemployment enters raw, so that each percentage point counts the same, or logged, so that each proportional rise counts the same and a rise from 4% to 8% counts as much as one from 10% to 20%. Both are defensible statements of how a crisis might act on framing, and the claim does not choose between them, so both stay on the curve. Growth takes negative values and enters raw only. Centring and standardising are not separate analyses, because shifting or rescaling the predictor cannot move t, r or p. The form carries almost none of the variance on the curve (`r pct(fk("pred_form"), 2)`), yet moving it alone changes the class of `r pct(fk("pred_form", "crossing_rate"))` of the pairs.

### Outcome family

The linear model fits the cell means directly; the beta family fits them through a logit link with a likelihood that respects the bounds of a share. Both describe the same conditional mean, and neither is a different answer to the claim. The bounds matter for the utilitarian scale, whose cell means come close to zero, while the cosmopolitan and positive cell means lie well inside the unit interval. The beta family barely moves the results: swapped into the specifications of the curve it leaves `r pct(dv("beta", "below_zero_sig"))` below zero with p < 0.05 under errors clustered by country, and its median shift in the aligned correlation is `r num(dv("beta", "median_shift"))`. It stays off the curve because clubSandwich, which computes the CR2 rule that classes the curve, does not cover beta regression, so keeping it would put two inference rules on one curve, and it serves instead as a check of the functional form, available for the share and the rate but not for the count, which is not a proportion.

### Inference

All the inference rules estimate the same slope and differ only in how uncertain they say it is. Conventional errors treat the 270 country-years as independent, which they are not, since in the reproduced model the residuals of a country correlate 0.53 from one year to the next, and the standard clustered errors (CR1, tested on 26 df) allow that correlation but overstate the evidence when a few of the 27 countries carry most of the variation that identifies the slope, as they do here. The curve is therefore classed by the CR2 correction of @BellMcCaffrey2002BiasReductionStandard, tested on Satterthwaite degrees of freedom in the form of @PustejovskyTipton2018SmallsampleMethodsClusterrobust, the correction adjusting the clustered errors for the unequal influence of the countries and the degrees of freedom, whose median on the curve is `r num(stats::median(curve$df_cr2), 1)`, saying how many countries effectively carry the information; [the module on panel data](companion/panel-data.qmd#sec-inference) sets out the three rules.

@tbl-inference gives the reproduced specification under each rule. The partial correlation stays the same throughout, but the p-value runs from `r num(inf("fe_twoway", "conventional", "p"), 5)` under conventional errors to `r num(inf("fe_twoway", "cr2_satterthwaite", "p"), 4)` under CR2, which is why the course does not call the reproduced result significant at 5% without saying under which errors. Across the curve, the share of specifications below zero with p < 0.05 is `r pct(sig_rule("p_conv"))` under conventional errors, `r pct(sig_rule("p_cr1"))` under CR1 and `r pct(sig_rule("p_cr2"))` under CR2.

| Rule | t | df | p | r from the conversion formula |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Conventional | `r num(inf("fe_twoway", "conventional", "t"))` | `r inf("fe_twoway", "conventional", "df")` | `r num(inf("fe_twoway", "conventional", "p"), 5)` | `r num(inf("fe_twoway", "conventional", "r_formula"))` |
| Clustered by country, CR1 | `r num(inf("fe_twoway", "cr1_g1", "t"))` | `r inf("fe_twoway", "cr1_g1", "df")` | `r num(inf("fe_twoway", "cr1_g1", "p"))` | `r num(inf("fe_twoway", "cr1_g1", "r_formula"))` |
